preconditioning.notes: Page: can be started manually or automatically by setting a fast-charging station as the navigation destination.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Toyota chief engineer (via InsideEVs): bZ "still runs on a 400-volt electrical architecture". Autopian gives the 57.7 kWh pack as 288.6 V.

capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Toyota Canada: "A 57.7-kWh battery will also be available on a XLE FWD model" (total, usable not stated). US release says the same.

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists 54.0 kWh usable for the 57.7 kWh bZ4X FWD pack (European MY25 listing of the same pack). Toyota states only total capacity.

chemistry.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists an NMC cathode for the 57.7 kWh pack (European MY25 listing of the same pack); 288.6 V from 78 cells = 3.7 V per cell, NMC class (Autopian, Toyota UK press pack). No manufacturer page states the chemistry of this pack, and EVKX reportedly shows LFP on one page (unverified; EVKX is blocked and was not read).

Estimated: GreenCars relays Toyota's chief engineer: 'no change to the cell chemistry' (nickel-manganese-cobalt cathodes) for the 2026 bZ, whose lineup includes the 57.7 kWh XLE FWD; not stated for the 57.7 kWh pack specifically.

ac_max_kw.notes: 11 kW on-board AC charger. Page says "across all trims".

published_10_80_min.notes: "around 30 minutes" under ideal DC fast-charging conditions; model-level claim, not per trim.

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists 150 kW DC maximum for the 57.7 kWh pack (European MY25 listing of the same pack); no Toyota page states a peak for this pack.

Estimated: No page states a peak for the 57.7 kWh pack; InsideEVs relays Toyota's chief engineer that the bZ is 'capped at 150 kilowatts' and EV Database lists 150 kW for the 57.7 kWh pack (European listing).
